product_context.name: Game Stream Highlight Analyzer
product_context.description: A modular web-based tool for identifying, scoring, and exporting high-impact moments from game streams using multi-source data.
key_features: Drag-and-drop interface for importing industrial input bundles.
Interactive timeline for visualizing and selecting highlights.
Real-time scoring and filtering based on user-defined criteria.
Collaboration tools for sharing and reviewing highlight selections.

modules.responsibility: Handle the import and preprocessing of industrial input bundles.
Score and rank moments based on multi-source data.
Filter and sort highlights based on user-defined criteria.
Export filtered highlights as downloadable files.
Persist working data locally and reload it on page load.
Render records and summaries to the user interface.
Handle user input from forms and bind DOM events.
Integrate all modules and manage application logic.

ux_contract.design_goal: A clear product workbench for stream/video operators, not a raw form dump. Prioritize scanability, obvious ownership of each control, and progressive complexity.

test_strategy.description: Test individual modules for correctness (e.g., data ingestion, scoring engine).
Ensure seamless interaction between modules (e.g., scoring engine and filtering module).
Gather feedback from streamers and editors on usability and accuracy.
Test the tool's ability to handle large datasets without significant lag.

acceptance_criteria: The project must run locally from index.html using `python -m http.server`.
Provide a real JSON import path using FileReader and/or a textarea; imported data must be processed by the app.
Implement a real scoring function and sort detected items by score descending in executable JavaScript.
Provide visible filter controls and executable filter logic for the requested fields.
Provide a manual marker form/control that appends a new item to the working dataset and rerenders results.
Provide a real export action using Blob, URL.createObjectURL, an anchor download, and the current filtered result set.
Persist working data locally with localStorage and reload it on page load.
Use domain fields such as streamer, game, timestamp/time, category, intensity, chatRate, keywords, title, description, and score.
